title: INFWAD – Express stickers
description: De belangrijkste onderwerpen van de Express-stickers (Express les 1 t/m 3, inclusief de ORM-les), uit de uitleg, de quizvragen, de oefentaken en de woordenlijst. Vragen, antwoorden en uitleg zijn in het Engels.

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.text: What is **Express**?
questions.explanation: Node is the engine, Express the car around it, TypeScript the lane assist.

options.text: A framework on top of Node.js that makes routing, responses and middleware simple

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.text: In the Express project (ESM) you write `import homeRouter from "./routes/home.routes.js"`, although the file is `home.routes.ts`. Why `.js`?
questions.explanation: ESM = the modern import/export module system, switched on with "type": "module" in package.json.

options.text: With ESM, local imports end in `.js`, even for `.ts` files
It's a typo: it should be `.ts`

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.text: What does `app.listen(3000)` do?
questions.explanation: Without it, nothing can connect. The port is the door into the server.

options.text: It starts the server so it can receive requests on port 3000

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.text: In `app.get("/", (req, res) => { ... })`, {{1}} holds what the browser asked, and {{2}} is how you answer.
questions.explanation: req: req.method, req.url, req.params, req.body. res: res.send, res.status, res.sendFile, res.render.

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.text: Where must the 404 handler go?
questions.explanation: Express checks top to bottom, so the 404 catches only what nothing else answered. Put it above app.get("/") and even / gives a 404.

options.text: At the end, after all other routes

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.explanation: Chain it: res.status(404).send(…). The status code tells the browser it wasn't found.

options.text: Move it to the top of the file

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.explanation: Without next(), the request stops in the middleware and the browser keeps waiting.

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.explanation: In a routes file you use the router, not the app.

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.text: With `app.use("/shop", productRouter)`, which URL reaches `router.get("/products")`?
questions.explanation: The first argument of app.use is a prefix for all routes in that router: the street name, the route is the house number.

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.text: What does `path.join(__dirname, "..", "views", "products.html")` do?
questions.explanation: path.join glues folder names into a path the right way for every operating system.

options.text: It builds the full path to the file, one folder up and then into views

questions.title: Express 1 – Express basics
questions.explanation: Params are always strings.

options.text: The products need to be in a database

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text: What's **server-side rendering (SSR)**?
questions.explanation: Express with EJS is SSR. A Vue app is a SPA. SSR = the kitchen plates your food.

options.text: The server builds the full HTML page for each request
The browser builds the page with JavaScript
Pages are built once, at install time

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text: What's the difference between GET and POST?
questions.explanation: GET = asking a question (form data shows in the URL, like a search). POST = handing in a form (like a login).

options.text: GET asks the server for something; POST sends data to the server in the body of the request
GET is for images, POST for HTML
GET sends data in the body, POST in the URL

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text: Submitting a form with `method="post"` gives "Cannot POST /add-product". Why?
questions.explanation: Add router.post("/add-product", …) for the same path.

options.text: There's only a GET route for /add-product

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text: `req.body` is undefined after a form POST. What's missing?
questions.explanation: The body has to be parsed before routes can read it.

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text: What type are the values in `req.body` from a form?
questions.explanation: Even a number input arrives as "12". Convert with Number().

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text: In MVC, the {{1}} manages the data, the {{2}} is what the user sees, and the {{3}} handles the request in between.
questions.explanation: Model = the storeroom, View = the presentation, Controller = does the work.

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text: Which order matches the MVC flow?
questions.explanation: The controller asks the model for data and picks the view.

options.text: Request → route → controller → model → controller → view → response

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text:
What's wrong with this route?

```ts
router.get("/products", showProducts());
```
questions.explanation: Express should call the function later, when a request comes in. With () the server even crashes at startup.

options.text: `showProducts()` runs immediately during setup; write `showProducts` without `()`

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text: How do you tell Express to use EJS?
questions.explanation: And app.set("views", path.join(__dirname, "views")) says where the templates are.

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text: Which EJS tag prints a value?
questions.explanation: <% %> = do something (loops, ifs). <%= %> = show something, safely escaped.

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC and EJS
questions.text:
The page says "products is not defined". Why? ```ts res.render("products"); // products.ejs <% products.forEach(product => { %>

<%= product.name %>

<% }) %> ```
questions.explanation: Use res.render("products", { products: getAllProducts() }). The object's properties become variables in the template.

questions.title: Express 3 – ORM (TypeORM)
questions.text: What is an **ORM**?
questions.explanation: TypeORM is the TypeScript ORM of the course.

options.text: An Object-Relational Mapper: it translates between objects in your code and rows in database tables, and writes the SQL for you

questions.title: Express 3 – ORM (TypeORM)
questions.text: TypeORM says "No metadata for Product" and doesn't create the table. What's the likely fix?
questions.explanation: Forget an entity in the list and its table isn't made.

questions.title: Express 3 – ORM (TypeORM)
questions.text: Why is `synchronize: true` dangerous in production?
questions.explanation: Handy in development. Production uses migrations: controlled, reviewed database changes.

options.text: It changes tables automatically from your entities and can delete data

questions.title: Express 3 – ORM (TypeORM)
questions.text: The decorator {{1}} marks a class as a table, {{2}} makes a property a column, and {{3}} makes the auto-numbered primary key.
questions.explanation: A decorator is a @label that adds behaviour to a class or property.

questions.title: Express 3 – ORM (TypeORM)
questions.text: What's the difference between `find()` and `findOneBy({ id: 1 })`?
questions.explanation: With { where: { … } } find filters like SQL WHERE.

options.text: `find()` always returns an array; `findOneBy` returns one object

questions.title: Express 3 – ORM (TypeORM)
questions.explanation: Database calls are asynchronous: without await you get a Promise.
